items.stem: To keep a page out of the search index, the correct approach is to:

options.rationale: Blocking crawl can leave an already-known URL indexed and stops engines seeing a noindex.

options.text: Allow crawling and add a noindex directive
options.rationale: Correct: the page must be crawlable for the engine to read and honour the noindex.
Removing a sitemap entry does not deindex a page.

options.text: Add a canonical to another page
options.rationale: Canonical is a consolidation hint, not a reliable removal method.

items.explanation: Correct: the page must be crawlable for the engine to read and honour the noindex.

items.stem: A key page sitting eight clicks from the homepage is a problem mainly because:

options.text: Deep pages are always lower quality
options.rationale: Depth is about discoverability, not inherent quality.

options.text: Depth reduces crawl priority and link authority reaching the page
options.rationale: Correct: important pages should sit shallow so crawlers and authority reach them easily.

options.text: Search engines cannot render deep pages
options.rationale: Rendering is unrelated to click depth.
URL length is a separate concern from click depth.

items.explanation: Correct: important pages should sit shallow so crawlers and authority reach them easily.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about canonical and noindex tags are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A canonical tag tells search engines which version of similar pages to treat as primary
options.rationale: Correct: canonical consolidates duplicate or similar URLs to a preferred one.

options.text: noindex asks search engines to keep a crawlable page out of the index
options.rationale: Correct: noindex is the directive for excluding a page from the index.

options.text: A canonical reliably removes a page from the index
options.rationale: Canonical is a hint for consolidation, not a removal directive.

options.text: noindex and canonical mean exactly the same thing
options.rationale: They serve different purposes and should not be conflated.

items.explanation: Correct: canonical consolidates duplicate or similar URLs to a preferred one.; Correct: noindex is the directive for excluding a page from the index.
